newsitem.title: USA: Phila. mayor meets with local banks on tax dispute.
newsitem.headline: Phila. mayor meets with local banks on tax dispute.

text.p: Philadelphia Mayor Ed Rendell met with local bank officials for an hour Wednesday to try to defuse a growing controversy over the city's personal property tax, the mayor's spokesman said.
"I think it's fair to say we had a good discussion," spokesman Kevin Feeley said in a telephone interview. "They raised some issues that were of importance to them and of great concern to us."

The dispute centers on Philadelphia's collection of the personal property tax, which is assessed on investors' holdings in out-of-state companies. Several local banks in recent weeks have moved customer accounts and several hundred jobs out of the city in an effort to avoid the tax.

Most other local governments in Pennsylvania have stopped collecting the tax, in anticipation that the state Supreme Court will overturn it when it rules in a pending case challenging the tax's constitutionality.
Feeley said participants at Wednesday's meeting agreed to set up a working group to meet again on the dispute and try to hash out a solution.
Local banks involved in the talks included First Union National Bank, a unit of First Union Corp ; PNC Bank Corp; and Mellon Bank Corp.

Paul Levine, a spokesman for First Union, said the bank was "encouraged" by the initial discussions. "Our view is that there were some positive steps taken at the meeting," Levine said in a telephone interview. "We left the meeting encouraged."

Philadelphia Controller Jonathan Saidel this week called on the administration to scrap the tax entirely, but Rendell and city council leaders have so far not indicated whether they support that idea.
